What to do in your 20s
instead of partying every weekend
Go on small adventures. A hike, a cheap train to a nearby city, a night camping. You'll remember these weekends long after the parties are forgotten.
Learn a skill that pays. Coding, design, writing, a trade. A few hours every weekend can change your career within a year. Even one evening a week adds up.
Train for something. A 10k, a climbing grade, a strength goal. A target gives your weekends structure and your life energy. Sign up and the motivation follows.
Host dinners instead of going out. Cook for friends at home. You save money, the conversations are better and people never forget good evenings.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Saturday mornings feel better when you start them learning something.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Saturday mornings feel better when you start them learning something.

slides.texte_overlay: Volunteer once a month. Helping others gives perspective and meaning, and you meet the kind of people worth knowing. It's also the best way to feel useful.
Still go out sometimes, just not every weekend. Fun is part of your 20s. Balance is what makes both the fun and the growth last.
